target_clause: Implementations MUST support ephemeral key exchange sizes of at least 2048 bits for cipher suites that use ephemeral finite field Diffie-Hellman (DHE) (Section 8.1.2 of [TLS12] and 224 bits for cipher suites that use ephemeral elliptic curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDHE) [RFC8422].

target_clause: To speed up handshake completion under these conditions, an endpoint MAY, for a limited number of occasions per each connection, send a packet containing unacknowledged CRYPTO data earlier than the PTO expiry, subject to the address validation limits in Section 8.1 of [QUIC-TRANSPORT].
previous_clause: When a client receives Handshake or 1-RTT packets prior to obtaining Handshake keys, it may assume some or all of the server's Initial packets were lost.
next_clause: Doing so at most once for each connection is adequate to quickly recover from a single packet loss.

target_clause: A server MAY discard 0-RTT keys earlier if it determines that it has received all 0-RTT packets, which can be done by keeping track of missing packet numbers.
previous_clause: After receiving a 1-RTT packet, servers MUST discard 0-RTT keys within a short time; the RECOMMENDED time period is three times the Probe Timeout (PTO, see [QUIC-RECOVERY]).

target_clause: Specifically, implementaions MUST attempt to enforce a maximum ack delay to avoid causing the peer spurious timeouts.
previous_clause: QUIC SHOULD delay sending acknowledgements in response to packets, but MUST NOT excessively delay acknowledgements of packets containing frames other than ACK or ACN_ECN.
next_clause: The RECOMMENDED maximum ack delay in QUIC is 25ms.

target_clause: A server MAY ignore a received Upgrade header field if it wishes to continue using the current protocol on that connection.
previous_clause: A client MAY send a list of protocol names in the Upgrade header field of a request to invite the server to switch to one or more of the named protocols, in order of descending preference, before sending the final response.
next_clause: Upgrade cannot be used to insist on a protocol change.

target_clause: If a HEADERS frame is received whose stream identifier field is 0x0, the recipient MUST respond with a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
previous_clause: HEADERS frames MUST be associated with a stream.
next_clause: The HEADERS frame changes the connection state as described in [FieldBlock].

target_clause: Intermediaries that process HTTP requests or responses (i.e., any intermediary not acting as a tunnel) MUST NOT forward a malformed request or response.
previous_clause: A response that is defined as never having content, even when a Content-Length is present, can have a non-zero Content-Length field even though no content is included in DATA frames.
next_clause: Malformed requests or responses that are detected MUST be treated as a stream error ([errors]) of type H3_MESSAGE_ERROR.

target_clause: A client MUST treat receipt of a PUSH_PROMISE frame that contains a larger Push ID than the client has advertised as a connection error of H3_ID_ERROR.
previous_clause: A server MUST NOT use a Push ID that is larger than the client has provided in a MAX_PUSH_ID frame ([frame-max-push-id]).
next_clause: A server MAY use the same Push ID in multiple PUSH_PROMISE frames.

target_clause: An origin server MUST send a Date header field in all other cases.
previous_clause: An origin server MAY send a Date header field if the response is in the 1xx (Informational) or 5xx (Server Error) class of status codes.
next_clause: A recipient with a clock that receives a response message without a Date header field MUST record the time it was received and append a corresponding Date header field to the message's header section if it is cached or forwarded downstream.

target_clause: o A client that receives a 417 (Expectation Failed) status code in response to a request containing a 100-continue expectation SHOULD repeat that request without a 100-continue expectation, since the 417 response merely indicates that the response chain does not support expectations (e.g., it passes through an HTTP/1.0 server).
previous_clause: Furthermore, since 100 (Continue) responses cannot be sent through an HTTP/1.0 intermediary, such a client SHOULD NOT wait for an indefinite period before sending the content.

target_clause: A proxy MAY transform the content of a message that does not contain a no-transform cache-control directive.
previous_clause: Note that this does not include changes to the message body that do not affect the content, such as transfer codings (Section 7 of [HTTP11]).
next_clause: A proxy that transforms the content of a 200 (OK) response can inform downstream recipients that a transformation has been applied by changing the response status code to 203 (Non-Authoritative Information) ([status.203]).

target_clause: If false, it is still acceptable for an ack to be received for this packet. However, a caller MUST NOT set is_retransmittable to true if an ack is not expected.
previous_clause: The retransmittability of various QUIC frames is described in [QUIC-TRANSPORT].
next_clause: sent_bytes: The number of bytes sent in the packet.

target_clause: A PRIORITY frame MAY identify a Stream Dependency ID using a Stream ID of 0; as in [RFC7540], this makes the request dependent on the root of the dependency tree.
previous_clause: Setting the PUSH_PRIORITIZED or PUSH_DEPENDENT flag causes the Prioritized Request ID or Stream Dependency ID (respectively) to identify a server push using a Push ID (see [frame-push-promise] for details).
next_clause: A PRIORITY frame MUST identify a client-initiated, bidirectional stream.

target_clause: kDelayedAckTimeout (RECOMMENDED 25ms):: The length of the peer’s delayed ack timer.
previous_clause: kMinRTOTimeout (RECOMMENDED 200ms):: Minimum time in the future an RTO timer may be set for.
next_clause: kInitialRtt (RECOMMENDED 100ms):: The RTT used before an RTT sample is taken.

target_clause: If QUIC needs to retransmit that data, it MUST use the same keys even if TLS has already updated to newer keys.
previous_clause: Each chunk of data that is produced by TLS is associated with the set of keys that TLS is currently using.
next_clause: Each encryption level corresponds to a packet number space.

target_clause: A sender SHOULD generate RWS as a single SP.
previous_clause: The RWS rule is used when at least one linear whitespace octet is required to separate field tokens.
next_clause: OWS and RWS have the same semantics as a single SP.

target_clause: Unless another mechanism is used for agreeing on an application protocol, endpoints MUST use ALPN for this purpose.
previous_clause: TLS uses Application Layer Protocol Negotiation ([ALPN]) to select an application protocol.
next_clause: When using ALPN, endpoints MUST immediately close a connection (see Section 10.2 of [QUIC-TRANSPORT]) with a no_application_protocol TLS alert (QUIC error code 0x178; see [tls-errors]) if an application protocol is not negotiated.

target_clause: A SETTINGS frame with a length other than a multiple of 6 octets MUST be treated as a connection error of type FRAME_SIZE_ERROR.
previous_clause: A badly formed or incomplete SETTINGS frame MUST be treated as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.

target_clause: A packet sent on an RTO alarm MUST NOT be blocked by the sender’s congestion controller.
previous_clause: Since this packet is sent as a probe into the network prior to establishing any packet loss, prior unacknowledged packets SHOULD NOT be marked as lost.
next_clause: A sender MUST however count these bytes as additional bytes in flight, since this packet adds network load without establishing packet loss.

target_clause: A proxy MUST forward unrecognized header fields unless the field name is listed in the Connection header field ([field.connection]) or the proxy is specifically configured to block, or otherwise transform, such fields.
previous_clause: New fields can be introduced without changing the protocol version if their defined semantics allow them to be safely ignored by recipients that do not recognize them; see [fields.extensibility].
next_clause: Other recipients SHOULD ignore unrecognized header and trailer fields.

target_clause: This MUST be set to zero on the first header block sequence, and incremented on each header block.
previous_clause: Sequence Number:: Present only on the first frame of a header block sequence.
next_clause: The next frame on the same stream after a HEADERS frame without the EHB flag set MUST be another HEADERS frame.

target_clause: A CONNECT request MUST be constructed as follows:
previous_clause: In HTTP/2 and HTTP/3, the CONNECT method is used to establish a tunnel over a single stream.
next_clause: The ":method" pseudo-header field is set to "CONNECT"

target_clause: Upon timeout, the sender MUST retransmit all unacknowledged CRYPTO data by calling RetransmitAllUnackedHandshakeData().
previous_clause: When CRYPTO frames are sent, the sender SHOULD set a timer for the handshake timeout period.
next_clause: On each consecutive expiration of the handshake timer without receiving an acknowledgement for a new packet, the sender SHOULD double the handshake timeout and set a timer for this period.

target_clause: For unexpected closures caused by error conditions, a QUIC CONNECTION_CLOSE or APPLICATION_CLOSE frame MUST be used.
previous_clause: For example, if an HTTP client sends a POST at the same time that a server closes a QUIC connection, the client cannot know if the server started to process that POST request if the server does not send a GOAWAY frame to indicate what streams it might have acted on.
next_clause: However, a GOAWAY MAY be sent first to provide additional detail to clients and to allow the client to retry requests.
